binders: For every natural number m, including m = 0.
For every real m × m matrix A = coefficient, indexed by i,j ∈ Fin m.
For every function f = profile : R → R.
For every real number d = profile' and every real number c = speed.
For every vector v = eigenvector ∈ R^m, represented by a function Fin m → R.
For every pair of real numbers x and t.
hypotheses: Av = cv: for every i ∈ Fin m, Σ(j ∈ Fin m) A(i,j)v(j) = c v(i).
The scalar function f has ordinary real derivative d at the point x - ct.
conclusions: For q(ξ,τ) = f(ξ - cτ)v, there exist vectors qt ∈ R^m and qx ∈ R^m such that all three conditions hold: τ ↦ q(x,τ) has derivative qt at t; ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) has derivative qx at x; and qt + A qx = 0.
Equivalently, the two partial derivatives of q exist at (x,t), and for every i ∈ Fin m, ∂q_i/∂t(x,t) + Σ(j ∈ Fin m) A(i,j) ∂q_j/∂x(x,t) = 0.

The existential quantifier for qt precedes that for qx. The witnesses are chosen for the given m, A, f, d, c, v, x, t and hypotheses; qx is quantified within the scope of qt. No single pair of vectors is required to serve all points.
mathematical_definitions: R^m means the real vector space of functions on {0,...,m-1}, with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication and the finite product topology.
Matrix-vector multiplication is (Aw)(i) = Σ(j ∈ Fin m) A(i,j)w(j).
The function q : R × R → R^m is defined by q(ξ,τ)(i) = f(ξ - cτ)v(i). The first argument is the spatial variable and the second is the temporal variable.

Having derivative w at a real point a means that the difference quotient tends to w as the real increment tends to zero through nonzero values, in the usual real topology or the product topology on R^m as appropriate.
The zero in the conclusion is the zero vector, with every coordinate equal to real zero.
The symbol profile' denotes a specified real derivative value at one point, not a derivative function.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every nonnegative integer m, real m × m matrix A, scalar function f on all of R, real numbers d and c, vector v in R^m, and real point (x,t), if Av = cv and f is differentiable at x - ct with derivative d, then q(ξ,τ) = f(ξ - cτ)v has both partial derivatives at (x,t) and satisfies ∂q/∂t(x,t) + A ∂q/∂x(x,t) = 0. Formally, this means there exist derivative vectors qt and qx for the temporal and spatial slices at that point, respectively, satisfying qt + A qx = 0.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: There is no assumption m > 0. For m = 0, the vector space contains only the empty vector, the eigenvector relation is automatic, and the coordinate equations are vacuous.

Despite the binder name eigenvector, v is not required to be nonzero. For v = 0, Av = cv holds for every A and c, and q is identically zero. The stated differentiability hypothesis on f is still present.
Consequently, the statement does not by itself assert that c is an eigenvalue in the convention requiring a nonzero eigenvector.
The speed c can be any real number, including zero and negative numbers.
The matrix A is a fixed real matrix, independent of space and time. No symmetry, diagonalizability, invertibility, spectral completeness, or hyperbolicity is assumed.
The profile is defined on all of R, but differentiability is assumed only at x - ct. There is no global differentiability or continuity-of-derivative assumption.

The asserted equation holds at the specified point under its pointwise hypothesis. The target does not assert that q solves the equation at every point without further differentiability assumptions on f.
The derivatives are full real derivatives of one-variable slices, not one-sided derivatives, derivatives within a restricted set, or weak or distributional derivatives.
The conclusion does not explicitly specify formulas qt = (-c*d)v and qx = d*v, although these follow from the given construction and differentiability hypothesis.
No initial or boundary conditions, uniqueness, nontriviality of q, or representation of all solutions are encoded.
For inputs failing either hypothesis, the implication makes no claim that the conclusion holds.
